pods.description:
Will Robert F. Kennedy Jr. win the 2028 Republican presidential nomination?: ArAIstotle YES 0.13 | mkt 0.49 | market_overpricing_yes | THIN | RRI 62/RFS 65

This market resolves YES only if RFK Jr. actually wins and accepts the Republican Party’s 2028 presidential nomination; cabinet service, endorsements, or buzz do not satisfy that trigger. The strongest dated evidence still cuts the other way: RFK Jr. is officially serving as HHS secretary and is listed as an Independent, not a Republican candidate, on his HHS bio and biography pages (HHS, “Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.”, https://www.hhs.gov/about/leadership/robert-kennedy.html; Wikipedia snapshot, “Robert F. Kennedy Jr.”, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.). He also publicly said on 2025-08-15 that he would not run in 2028, and Cheryl Hines reiterated on 2025-12-09 that “he’s not going to run” (ABC News, 2025-08-15, “Amid criticism from Laura Loomer, RFK Jr. says he won't run for president in 2028”, https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/amid-criticism-laura-loomer-rfk-jr-run-president/story?id=124684850; The Guardian, 2025-12-09, “Cheryl Hines says Robert F Kennedy Jr won’t run for president in 2028”, https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/dec/09/cheryl-hines-rfk-jr-run-president-2028). As of 2026-08-15, researchers also did not find a clear FEC 2028 presidential candidacy record (FEC candidate search, https://www.fec.gov/data/candidates/?q=Robert%20Kennedy). The best YES case is that he endorsed Trump in 2024 and remains visible inside Republican politics, including reported campaigning in Iowa with Republicans, which could keep a future lane open; but that is still far from winning an official GOP nomination (Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.; X post by @Alpha_Omega_LLC, https://x.com/i/web/status/2086962614345564310; X post by @RieuDu41557, https://x.com/i/web/status/2086705736915070990). News and X broadly agree he is politically adjacent to the GOP, but verified reporting is much more negative on an actual 2028 run than the speculative social chatter, so we weight the reporting more. A useful prior lesson here is not to mistake endorsement or proximity to power for actually winning a contested nomination, which keeps our estimate well below the market price.

pods.name: Will Iran target a Arab country on August 18, 2026?
pods.description:
Will Iran target a Arab country on August 18, 2026?: ArAIstotle YES 0.489575 | mkt 0.0245 | market_underpricing_yes | DEEP | RRI 38/RFS 60

This market asks whether, on 2026-08-18 AST, Iran carried out a qualifying air strike or surface-to-surface missile strike directed at an Arab country. The strongest on-contract evidence is the UAE government’s statement that its air defences detected two ballistic missiles on 2026-08-18 and that its assessment showed they were launched from Iran; Reuters reported that directly, which fits the contract’s requirement that the action be confirmed to have originated from Iranian territory and notes that interception does not disqualify it (Reuters, 2026-08-18, "UAE says two missiles detected earlier were launched from Iran", https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/uae-says-iran-launched-two-missiles-it-2026-08-18/). The main weakening point is target ambiguity: the contract requires the strike be directed at the terrestrial territory or internal waters of a listed Arab country, and available reporting does not independently pin down the flight path or impact point; Al Jazeera also reports Tehran denied targeting the UAE (Al Jazeera liveblog, 2026-08-18, https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/8/18/iran-war-live-trump-rejects-mou-extension-as-us-claims-control-of-hormuz). Exclusion check: I am not relying on proxy attacks, cyber activity, artillery, or mere threats, and intercepted ballistic missiles can still count under the written rules. News and X broadly agree that the UAE attributed two ballistic missiles to Iran, but the X detail that they targeted maritime traffic and fell into the sea comes from low-trust posts, so verified reporting carries more weight than social chatter (e.g. @A_M_R_M1, 2026-08-18, https://x.com/i/web/status/2089804439360360766). A prior lesson that applies here is not to discount a confirmed, dated on-contract event just because some details remain contested; that pushes our estimate above the market price, though not to certainty because the “directed at UAE territory/internal waters” element is still not cleanly confirmed.

pods.name: US announces end of Iranian blockade by September 30, 2026?

US announces end of Iranian blockade by September 30, 2026?: ArAIstotle YES 0.62 | mkt 0.345 | market_underpricing_yes | DEEP | RRI 35/RFS 40

This market needs a very specific trigger by 2026-09-30: an official US-government statement, through official channels, that clearly and unambiguously ends, lifts, terminates, or suspends the naval blockade in general. There is no doubt the blockade exists in the relevant period: CNN and NPR reported the US military reimposed it on 2026-07-14, and later White House and Reuters-linked coverage still had Trump describing US control over Hormuz and a continuing blockade through 2026-08-12 (CNN, 2026-07-14, "July 14, 2026 — US naval blockade of Iranian ports goes into effect", https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/14/world/live-news/iran-war-trump; NPR, 2026-07-14, "U.S. starts blockade on Iran as Hormuz Strait standoff escalates", https://www.npr.org/2026/07/14/nx-s1-5893257/us-iran-updates; White House, 2026-07-28, "President Trump on Fox & Friends...", https://www.whitehouse.gov/releases/2026/07/president-trump-on-fox-friends-americas-unrelenting-strength-keeps-maximum-pressure-on-iran/; Reuters item via Google News, 2026-08-12, "Trump says US has 'total control' over Strait of Hormuz", https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilwFBVV95cUxOS2o4cWFmWUZQNXN2WUhmYU1GVFpxdk9WM3d1YzhtS3lkQVpFdUoyNjJZMG9oSXpRNkk2VXM3X2FlTXp2T2V2VldGR3dBMGczQ0JQQkM2YjJTT2VkRkFBMVpOamlFNTBocGtvR2ZJUWJ2TnRtYVhnTVMzM1RkRks0MzV0MFQ5RWxrdmlTZThMUXh1emc). The main YES case is that the US has already shown it can make a qualifying announcement fast: CENTCOM said on 2026-06-18 it had lifted the blockade, and the White House on 2026-06-19 said the deal reopened Hormuz to free navigation, which fits the contract’s focus on announcement over implementation (Al Jazeera, 2026-06-18, "US military says it has lifted naval blockade of Iranian ports", https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/6/18/us-military-says-it-has-lifted-naval-blockade-of-iranian-ports; White House, 2026-06-19, "President Trump’s Iran Agreement Is America First in Action", https://www.whitehouse.gov/releases/2026/06/president-trumps-iran-agreement-is-america-first-in-action/). But those June statements are outside this market’s window, so they only show plausibility, not settlement. News and X are aligned that the blockade remains in place; @AJEnglish likewise posted on 2026-08-10 that Trump said he would keep the blockade, and I weight the reporting more because it is official and attributable (https://x.com/i/web/status/2086614757277401393). One prior lesson matters here: by-date announcement markets can turn on a single official statement, so we price the remaining diplomatic window rather than treating today’s no-announcement state as final. Even so, absent any post-2026-07-14 qualifying announcement, our estimate stays a bit below the market price rather than embracing the market’s stronger YES lean.

pods.name: Will MegaETH perform an airdrop by December 31, 2026?

MegaETH’s official token page says Fluffle NFT holders received 50% of their MEGA automatically delivered to their wallets on 2026-04-30, which matches a token distribution to users rather than an NFT drop; The Block reported the MEGA token went live the same day and major exchanges opened spot trading, which matters because the market excludes locked or non-swappable tokens (MegaETH, 2026, “MEGA | MegaETH”, https://www.megaeth.com/token; The Block, 2026-04-30, “MegaETH token goes live as major exchanges open MEGA trading”, https://www.theblock.co/news/defi/2026-04-30-megaeth-token-goes-live-as-major-exchanges-open-mega-trading-399563). The main caveat is that some other allocations involved claim/vesting mechanics, so not every cohort is clean airdrop evidence; but the Fluffle auto-delivery plus live trading appears sufficient on the written criteria. News reporting and X chatter broadly agree the token already launched; X posts like @Richmanvn referring to MegaETH as an already-completed airdrop are only soft corroboration, and we weight the official site and reporting much more highly (X, @Richmanvn, 2026-08-14, https://x.com/i/web/status/2088095135972405703). The prior lesson applied here is simple: for a “by-date” crypto market, once a dated in-window qualifying event is documented, you should resolve toward YES rather than waiting for fresher news.

The relevant prior lesson is that by-date IPO markets often overread filing progress; what matters here is whether trading actually starts by year-end. Because verified reporting is mixed rather than decisive, we weight news far more than X and stay below the market’s very bullish Democratic price. A useful prior lesson here is to avoid getting pinned to an aggressive market favorite when there is no contract-settling fact yet; this market will be decided by seats or, if necessary, the Speaker, and today’s evidence still looks competitive rather than settled.

The main NO argument is contractual ambiguity: the rules exclude pauses limited to specific targets or locations, and later Reuters/BBC reporting shows the war plainly continued, so adjudicators could in theory decide this was too short or too imperfect to count (Reuters, 2026-05-08, “Trump hopes for extension to agreed three-day Ukraine-Russia ceasefire”, https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-ukraine-accuse-each-other-violating-ceasefire-2026-05-08/; BBC, 2026-08-13, “Major Russian grain export terminals hit in Ukraine Black Sea port attack”, https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c5y49xp2wrno?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss). But the cited May deal was framed as a general stop to fighting, not a category-specific carveout, and violations after agreement do not undo the fact of agreement. News reporting is consistent on that; X chatter is mixed and much weaker, mostly generic debate about ceasefires rather than evidence against the May agreement, so we weight the reporting far more heavily (e.g. @sokolovkereal, 2026-08-09, https://x.com/i/web/status/2086319882673803373). The key prior lesson applied is that once a confirmed, dated, on-contract event is in the record, it should not be heavily discounted just because the market price is low; here we still trim the estimate because the recognition clause creates a real edge-case for resolution.

pods.name: US announces end of Iranian blockade by August 12, 2026?

US announces end of Iranian blockade by August 12, 2026?: ArAIstotle YES 0.48524999999999996 | mkt 0.0005 | market_underpricing_yes | DEEP | RRI 38/RFS 34

This market asks a backward-looking question: between market creation on 2026-08-07 and the 2026-08-12 deadline, did the U.S. government or an authorized official publicly and officially announce a general end, lifting, termination, or suspension of the naval blockade? The main weakness is that some wording sounds phased or conditional—“begin removing” and “within 30 days”—and the U.S. later reimposed the blockade on 2026-07-14, showing ambiguity about whether the June statements were a clear present suspension (CENTCOM, 2026-07-13, “U.S. Forces to Resume Naval Blockade Against Iran”, https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PUBLIC-RELEASES/Article/4542098/us-forces-to-resume-naval-blockade-against-iran/ ; CNN, 2026-07-14, live coverage, https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/14/world/live-news/iran-war-trump). Still, the contract explicitly says later reversal does not matter once a qualifying announcement is made, and the fact-check record independently classified the claim as true based on a public U.S. announcement before 2026-08-12. News reporting and X chatter broadly agree that “lift the blockade” was a live policy issue, but I weight the official White House/BBC/CENTCOM record far above unverified posts like @Osint613 because settlement turns on official U.S. communication, not online sentiment (https://x.com/i/web/status/2086718149588598859). pods.name: The Calculated Climber
pods.description:
Type: Balanced risk, controlled upside seeker

Short description: This player is willing to take risk, but only in a structured way. They push for a better multiplier, but do not lose control.

Analysis of the footage: The player begins calmly and makes several moves with consistent timing. They do not instantly cash out after the first win, but they also do not recklessly push until the end. After reaching a meaningful multiplier, the player pauses, evaluates the position, and cashes out before the risk becomes too high.
This is a balanced risk profile. The player shows confidence, but not impulsiveness. They are comfortable taking multiple steps, but they still respect the danger zone. The decision speed stays consistent, which suggests the player is not emotionally reacting to every move.

pods.name: The Full Degen
pods.description:
Type: High-risk, low discipline, maximum volatility

Short description: This player is not here to manage risk. This player is here for glory, pain, content, and maybe spiritual damage.

Analysis of the footage: The player enters with a large bet relative to the visible balance and immediately starts moving fast. There is little to no hesitation before each step. The player ignores safe cashout opportunities and continues pushing even after reaching a strong multiplier.
The footage shows extremely high volatility preference and almost no stop-loss discipline. The player is not responding to risk in a controlled way. They are chasing the maximum outcome. If they win, it looks heroic. If they lose, it looks completely predictable.
The key signal is not only the high-risk action, but the lack of adjustment. Even when the risk becomes obvious, the player keeps going. This indicates aggressive risk appetite, low caution, and strong reward fixation.

pods.name: The Momentum Chaser
pods.description:
Type: Win-reactive, emotionally aggressive

Short description: This player becomes more aggressive after early success. A win gives them confidence, and confidence quickly turns into “I am him.”

Analysis of the footage: The player starts with a normal bet and makes the first few moves carefully. After the multiplier grows and the run looks good, their behavior changes. The pauses become shorter, the decisions become faster, and the player starts pushing deeper than they originally seemed comfortable with.
This is a classic momentum-driven pattern. The player is not reckless from the beginning, but winning changes their risk tolerance. The footage shows clear risk escalation after positive feedback. The longer the run goes well, the more confident the player becomes, and the more likely they are to ignore a reasonable cashout point.

pods.name: The Safe Walker
pods.description:
Type: Low-risk, capital protection first

Short description: This player is careful, disciplined, and more focused on not losing than maximizing upside. They take small wins early and avoid letting greed take over.

Analysis of the footage: The player starts with a modest bet size and takes time before the first move. After crossing one or two steps, they hesitate briefly, check the multiplier, and cash out early even though there is clearly more upside available. The key signal is that the player does not chase a bigger payout. They accept a small profit and leave safely.
You can see strong stop-loss discipline here. The player is not trying to “beat the game.” They are trying to survive the game. Even after a successful early move, they do not become more aggressive. This behavior suggests low volatility preference, high caution, and strong capital protection.
